component.name: Vocem Overlay
component.summary: Discord voice overlay drawn inside the game

description.p: Vocem Overlay shows who is talking in your Discord voice channel inside the game itself, rather than in a window on top of it. A Vulkan layer puts it there, and an OpenGL hook does the same for games that use OpenGL.

Because the overlay is part of the game's picture rather than a separate window, it is invisible on the desktop and it survives exclusive fullscreen. There are no per-game launch options to set, and no nested compositor.
This application sets the overlay up: position, size, opacity, pictures and who to show. It is not affiliated with Discord Inc.

description.p: Several ways a game went undetected are fixed: launched by Heroic, started through a wrapper script, installed in a Wine prefix, started over D-Bus, and anything running on GNOME.
A game started from a terminal, a script or the file manager is found through the desktop entry that runs it, and a game that is itself a Flatpak appears on the Applications page.
The settings window opens about two seconds faster.
The voice panel can be laid out horizontally, as a line of people along an edge of the screen, and the overlay can draw in any TrueType font installed on the machine.
The overlay's colours are right in games that render in sRGB. They were encoded a second time, which left the panel light grey instead of dark slate.
The text of a message now appears in a game that is itself a Flatpak, where only the sender's name and picture did.
The overlay now reaches games that are themselves Flatpaks, through a Vulkan layer extension and a bridge the daemon publishes across the sandbox.
First public release: Vulkan layer, OpenGL interposer, daemon and settings window.
